user.title: Connect to a Tapo H500
user.description: All traffic remains local. The TP-Link cloud password is required only for local media encryption.

data_description.poll_interval: How quickly activity reaches Home Assistant. This is the whole notification delay -- nothing arrives sooner than the next check. A check costs the hub about 40ms, so 2 seconds is comfortable and 1 is allowed. Changeable later under Configure.

reauth_confirm.title: Reconnect to your Tapo H500
reauth_confirm.description: The hub refused the stored credentials outright rather than simply failing to answer. Retype the camera account -- the local account made in the Tapo app, not the TP-Link email used to sign in to it. All traffic remains local; the TP-Link cloud password is still used only for local media encryption.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect or authenticate with the H500.
error.no_cameras: The H500 reported no paired cameras.

abort.reauth_successful: Reconnected. The stored credentials have been replaced.

data.keep_downloads: Downloaded clips to keep per camera
data.keep_rings: Doorbell presses to keep per camera
data.silent_hours: Hours of silence before a camera is flagged
data.keep_person: Recordings with a person to keep per camera
data.card_days: Days the cards show by default
data.auto_restart: Restart the hub automatically when its recording service fails

data_description.convert_mp4: MP4 plays in the browser; turn this off to keep the hub's original MPEG-TS.
data_description.keep_downloads: 0 keeps everything. Any other number prunes the oldest automatic downloads once a camera holds more than that. Manual downloads are never pruned.
data_description.poll_interval: The whole notification delay: nothing reaches Home Assistant sooner than the next check. About 40ms of hub time per check, so low values are cheap.
data_description.keep_rings: 0 treats presses like everything else. Any other number keeps that many of the newest presses whatever their age, so a busy afternoon of motion cannot evict the press that mattered.
data_description.silent_hours: A camera off the Wi-Fi or flat looks exactly like a quiet one: the hub reports no online flag and no battery, so silence is the only evidence there is. Lower this for a busy doorbell, raise it for a back gate that genuinely sees nobody all day. Capped at 24 because that is how far back the hub is asked.
data_description.keep_person: 0 treats them like everything else. Any other number keeps that many of the newest recordings with a person in them whatever their age, so a windy afternoon of motion cannot evict the one recording of somebody at the door. Counted separately from doorbell presses; a press with a person in it is protected by both.
data_description.download_types: Leave empty to download everything, which is what happens now. Tick a few and only recordings carrying one of them are kept -- the clips people go back for are usually the ones with a person or a doorbell press in them, not the traffic.
data_description.card_days: Cards without their own “Days to show” follow this; a card with one set keeps it.
data_description.auto_restart: Both known media failures are cured by a reboot and nothing else. At most one automatic restart every six hours, announced in the log and as a tapo_h500_auto_restart event. Cameras going quiet never triggers this — a reboot gains nothing against a flat battery.

faces.title: Name faces

layout.title: Camera layout

sensitivity.title: Unusual activity
sensitivity.description:
How busy a camera has to get before it counts as unusual, measured against its own recent rate rather than a fixed number.

**Sensitive** flags twice its typical hour. **Normal** three times. **Relaxed** five times, and needs more activity before it considers the question at all.

Set these per camera: three times typical is a busy afternoon on a doorbell facing a pavement, and somebody in the garden on a back gate.

abort.no_faces: The hub has not recognised any faces yet. It only reports one when its own face detection fires, and only for the period still held — try again after someone has been seen.
abort.one_camera: Only one camera is paired with this hub. A direction needs two places to be between.
abort.no_cameras: No cameras are paired with this hub yet.

trigger_type.loitering: {entity_name}: someone the hub does not recognise has waited there
trigger_type.possible_delivery: {entity_name}: a visit that looked like a delivery
trigger_type.prowling: Someone went round the house rather than up to the door
trigger_type.arrival: Someone you have named arrives home
trigger_type.visit: A visit begins (once per visitor, not once per recording)

storage_nearly_full.title: H500 storage is {used}% full
storage_nearly_full.description: The hub is about to start overwriting its oldest recordings to make room. Loop recording does not stop at full -- it discards the oldest footage silently. Download anything worth keeping, or format the hub storage once you have.

hub_unreachable.title: H500 is not responding
hub_unreachable.description: The hub has stopped answering, so nothing is being recorded to Home Assistant and every entity is showing its last known value. Check that it is powered and on the network. If the username is a TP-Link email rather than a local account, the hub refuses it with an error indistinguishable from being offline.

unnamed_face.title: A face the hub keeps seeing has no name
unnamed_face.description:
Face {face_id} has been seen {sightings} times on {cameras} and has not been named. Naming it makes every card, sensor and notification say who it is instead of a number — "Alice rang the Front Doorbell".

Name it under Configure → Name faces, where each face is listed with a link to its photograph, or with the Name this face button on the faces card.

{others} other face(s) are also waiting to be named.

init.title: Name this face
init.description: The hub keeps recognising face {face_id}. Give them a name and every card, sensor and notification will use it. Their photo is on the faces card if you need a look first. Submitting an empty box just closes this notice.

camera_silent.title: A camera has gone quiet
camera_silent.description:
{cameras} has recorded nothing for {hours} hours.

That usually means it is off the Wi-Fi, flat or unplugged, but it can also mean nothing has happened there. The hub cannot tell you which: its paired-device record has no online flag, no signal strength and no battery, so silence is the only evidence available. Every entity for that camera is still showing its last known value.

Check the camera, or raise the threshold under Configure → Settings if it is simply somewhere quiet.

clashing_camera_names.title: Two cameras share a name
clashing_camera_names.description:
More than one paired camera is called {cameras}, so their downloads are filed in the same folder.

Recordings are stored under a slug of the camera's own name, which is what makes "already downloaded" a check of the files on disk rather than a separate index that could disagree with them. Two cameras sharing a name means one camera's recording answers that question for the other, and clips from both appear under whichever card you open.

Rename one of them in the Tapo app. Anything already downloaded stays where it is; new recordings go to the new folder.

camera_tampered.title: A camera reported being interfered with
camera_tampered.description:
{camera} reported tampering at {when} ({count} report(s) in the last day).

This is the hub's own alarm for a camera being handled — knocked, covered, or lifted off its mount. It was confirmed on real hardware by taking a camera off its bracket, so it means what it says, but a knock or a strong gust can raise it too.

Worth checking rather than dismissing: everything else this integration reports happened outside the house, and this one is about the camera itself. If it is real, the recordings you will want are the ones after it — check that the camera is still pointing where it should and that its recent clips are on the hub.

It clears on its own once the report ages out of the last 24 hours.

media_wedged.title: The H500 has stopped serving recordings
media_wedged.description: The hub is still detecting events, but its media service has stopped delivering recordings — either refusing sessions outright, or answering them cleanly with no video in them. Notification photographs, previews and downloads will fail until it recovers, and in testing only a hub reboot clears either state: press the hub's Restart button on its device page, or power-cycle it. Recordings already on the hub are not lost.

downloads_failing.title: Recordings from {cameras} are not downloading
downloads_failing.description: {count} automatic downloads in a row have failed. The recordings still exist on the hub, but they will not appear in Home Assistant until this is fixed, and the hub will eventually overwrite them. The log (Settings → System → Logs, search “tapo_h500”) says why each one failed — a full disk and a missing ffmpeg are the usual reasons. This notice clears itself when a download succeeds.

restart_ineffective.title: Restarting the hub did not fix its recording service
restart_ineffective.description: The hub was restarted automatically and the failure came straight back — which has never happened before, so this is something new rather than the known wedge. Automatic restarts are paused until recordings serve again, so the evidence is not rebooted away. Download diagnostics from the integration's menu and open an issue with it; a power cycle (unplug, wait, replug) is worth one try, and if recordings recorded during the failure play as empty, say so — it means the video was never written.
